issue_context.title: Possible wrong global histogram after merging the partition statistics
issue_context.body:
![img_v3_029e_2a4ddc4e-edd6-44f4-946c-9936eabe1f2g](https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/assets/7846227/04524279-cca7-400d-a661-a86de296de4f)

After the `slices.SortFunc`, The order like `[2, 2], [1, 3], [2, 3]` will be a valid sorted result. And the following merging process just checks the bucket size. So it's possible that we treat the `[2, 2]` as the first global bucket and merge `[1, 3]` and `[2, 3]` as the second.

The merge result is wrong.

review_comments: Since this part of logic is very complicated, I suggest we add an assert here to make sure `upper == currentLeftMost` is true for all buckets in `[i,leftMostInvalidPosForNextRound-1]`.

As you can see the TopN of column a is only the value 1. But column a has three values 0, 1, and 2.
So the added bucket is an expected one.
Though it's not changed in this PR. Can we change it into `if !(original_check) { continue }` to make it easier to read?

Yes, i think this would be a better way.
My concern is that it may introduce more pressure on reviewing.
The result becomes more balanced compared with previous.
Considering the precision loss of int-float conversion and float calculation, please add some checks or asserts to make sure they are larger than `0`.
